notes: Split red lentils for shorbet adas and mujaddara-style dishes; cook fast (saves gas). Gaza price lists call them yellow lentils (عدس أصفر). Sub-type of the existing lentils item; a core aid-parcel staple.
Whole brown/green lentils (black lentils in Gaza price lists). Take longer to cook than split red lentils. Sub-type of the existing lentils item.
Egyptian-style split dry fava for taameya/falafel and bessara. Mostly arrives from Egypt.
Listed in Gaza market price lists (بازيلا ناشفة).

Sold dried by the kilo or ready-soaked in brine jars. Dried beans need days of soaking and boiling; the jarred ones are eaten as a snack. Sealed jars keep without refrigeration.

The standard breakfast. Plain, large-bean, small-bean and ready-mixed (Egyptian, Palestinian or Lebanese style, with chilli, lemon or tahini) cans. WFP parcels include canned beans. Gaza market price about 2 NIS a can (Oct 2025).
Boiled whole chickpeas. WFP ready-to-eat rations have included a can of chickpeas.
Ready-to-eat hummus in small cans. WFP parcels have included chickpea paste.
Ready-to-eat aubergine and tahini dip in cans.
Plain boiled white beans in brine. Aid parcels often carry canned beans.
Baked-bean style white beans in tomato sauce; can be eaten without cooking.
Used for bazella stew with rice when fresh vegetables are missing.
Gaza market price about 4 NIS a can (Oct 2025).
Imported whole or chopped tomatoes. Most Gaza households use tomato paste (existing tomato_paste item) instead.
Seen in Jordanian shops; availability in Gaza not confirmed.
In oil, in water or with chilli; chunks, flakes or shredded. Aid parcels have included canned tuna (often 2 cans per parcel). Gaza market price 2 to 4 NIS for a can of tuna or sardines (Oct 2025).
Tuna pre-mixed with corn, beans, vegetables or sauces. Ready to eat.
Includes 'mackerel sardine'. UNRWA has given extra canned sardines to the poorest families.

Sealed cans keep without refrigeration; once opened, eat the same day. Gaza market price about 10 NIS (Oct 2025). Al-Madaen (المدائن) luncheon is named in Gaza price lists, but no pack size was given.
Siniora sells a large 800 g can.
UNRWA parcels used to include canned meat and corned beef; it was later dropped from UNRWA baskets. Branded cans are sold in markets.
Shelf-stable sausages in cans or jars. Check the label: some chilled sausages look similar but need a fridge.
Local olives are cured at home or bought loose by weight. Jarred brands are also sold. Olives kept in brine or oil last months without a fridge.
Mostly sold sliced in jars or cans.
Jars are graded by count per jar (7-9, 18-25, 30-36). Pickles are also sold loose by the uqiya in Gaza.
Baby aubergine pickled in brine (not makdous in oil).
